title: 2.6.2 Group PA Part 2: Build It
description: Turn the chart you just passed into a documented, loop-driven program. Ten checks, all of them things Chapter 2 taught. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Fill in the header
steps.instructions: The top of script.js has three comment lines waiting: Problem, Partners, Date. Fill all three in. Both partners' names, on the Partners line, before anything else happens.

steps.title: Copy your pseudocode in as comments
steps.instructions: Your chart from 2.6.1, written out one instruction per line as // comments, indented to show what sits inside the loop and the decision. Do this before you write a single line of JavaScript. If a line does not say what you meant on the chart, fix the wording now.

steps.title: Declare the inputs and the limit
steps.instructions: One variable per number your problem takes in, plus one string for the name or label. Descriptive camelCase names -- itemsPerLocker, not p. The limit you are comparing against never changes, so declare it with const.
hints: The limit is the fixed number in your problem statement: 2.00, 15.00, 70, or the trip distance
const goodDealLimit = 2.00; -- const is what says it never moves, and the name stays camelCase like every other name
A name someone else can read is worth more marks here than a short one

steps.title: Set up the loop
steps.instructions: Write the for-loop header that walks your input range. Use the loop-setup hexagon from your chart as a guide: the initialization, the condition, and the step all go in the hexagon. The body of the loop is everything indented inside it.
hints: for (let i = 1; i <= n; i++) { -- the hexagon in your chart
If your problem uses a while loop, write the initialization, condition, and update as separate lines

steps.title: Add the continue
steps.instructions: Inside the loop, write the continue that skips the iterations your rule excludes. The continue goes BEFORE the flip/accumulate logic so the skipped iterations are truly skipped.
hints: The continue goes at the TOP of the loop body, before any flip logic

steps.title: Do the work inside the loop
steps.instructions: After the continue, write the logic that flips, accumulates, or counts. Name your variables for what they represent -- not what they store.
hints: balance = balance + deposit; -- not b = b + d

steps.title: Add the break or continue that the brief forces
steps.instructions: One of the four problems forces a break; one forces a continue. Make sure yours is there and clearly marked with a comment.
hints: Savings Run: break when balance >= target
Coin Drawer: break when drawer is empty
Locker Sweep and Word Audit: continue skips specific iterations

steps.title: Add the switch classification
steps.instructions: After the loop, write a switch that classifies the final state / outcome / denomination. Every case needs a break. The default handles the remaining case.
hints: Every case ends with break; default has no break

steps.title: Guard the bad input
steps.instructions: At the top of the program, before the loop, validate the one input that can be bad. Throw an Error with a descriptive message if it fails.
hints: if (n < 1) throw new Error('n must be at least 1');
The throw goes BEFORE the loop, so the loop never runs on bad input

steps.title: Read it back to each other
steps.instructions: Swap the keyboard. The partner who did not type reads the program out loud line by line while the other checks it against the chart. Every shape on the chart should appear once, in order. Fix what does not match, then run three sets of numbers through it -- you will need them for the demo writeup.

requirements.title: Both partners named in the header
requirements.description: The Partners line at the top of script.js has names on it
requirements.hint: Line 3 of script.js: // Partners: -- put both names after the colon.

requirements.title: The problem is named in the header
requirements.description: The Problem line says which of the four menu problems this is
requirements.hint: Line 2 of script.js: // Problem: -- Locker Sweep, Word Audit, Savings Run, or Coin Drawer.

requirements.title: The limit is a const
requirements.description: The number that never changes is declared with const, not let
requirements.hint: const goodDealLimit = 2.00; -- const rather than let, because it never changes. The name is camelCase like every other name.

requirements.title: A string variable is declared
requirements.description: One variable holds text -- the name or label your problem talks about
requirements.hint: Something like const pizzeriaName = "Tony's"; -- quotes make it a string.

requirements.title: A number variable is declared
requirements.description: At least one variable holds a number typed straight in
requirements.hint: let sliceCount = 8; -- no quotes around a number, or it is a string.

requirements.title: The loop uses a for or while
requirements.description: A for or while loop is present and walks the input range
requirements.hint: for (let i = 1; i <= n; i++) { or while (amount > 0) {

requirements.title: The loop has a continue
requirements.description: A continue statement appears inside the loop
requirements.hint: continue; -- exactly that word, inside the loop body.

requirements.title: A break AND a continue
requirements.description: The loop contains both a continue and a break, as the brief forces — one skip and one stop.
requirements.hint: Two keywords, both in the loop: continue for the iterations the rule excludes, break for the moment the outcome is decided.

requirements.title: A switch classifies the outcome
requirements.description: A switch with at least three cases (each with a break) and a default.
requirements.hint: Three case labels -- the lesson text says your classification names three outcomes -- every one closed with break, and a default that catches the rest.

requirements.title: The bad input is guarded with throw
requirements.description: A throw statement guards the bad input before the loop runs
requirements.hint: if (n < 1) throw new Error('n must be at least 1'); -- before the loop.
